records.document:
For FY2031, Auralis Treasury's liquidity covenant requires at least USD 2.50 million of unrestricted cash at year end. Restricted cash cannot be counted toward that minimum.

At FY2031 year end, Auralis Treasury held USD 2.75 million of unrestricted cash and USD 0.40 million of restricted cash.

For FY2030, the required unrestricted-cash minimum was USD 3.00 million.
records.hypothesis: Auralis Treasury satisfied its FY2031 minimum unrestricted-cash covenant at year end.

records.document:
The FY2032 operating-cost ratio for Brindle Services is defined as operating costs divided by service revenue, without adding financing costs.

Brindle Services reported FY2032 operating costs of USD 18 million and service revenue of USD 72 million. Financing costs were USD 3 million.

The FY2031 operating-cost ratio was 30 percent.
records.hypothesis: Brindle Services' FY2032 operating costs were exactly one quarter of its FY2032 service revenue.

records.document:
A delivery of at most 75 kilograms of the catalyst is exempt from the certified-supervisor requirement. A delivery above 75 kilograms requires a certified supervisor.

The Solmere delivery contains exactly 0.075 metric tonnes of the catalyst. One metric tonne equals 1000 kilograms.

The delivery arrived on 14 March 2033; its packaging weighs 6 kilograms and is excluded from the stated catalyst mass.
records.hypothesis: The Solmere catalyst delivery is exempt from the certified-supervisor requirement.

records.document:
Velden must not provide the pricing schedule to outside parties, except that Velden may provide it to the annual auditor during a board-approved access window of no more than 2 days.

The board approved the annual auditor's pricing-schedule access from 10 June 2034 through 11 June 2034, inclusive. Those dates form a 2-day access window.

The board did not authorize access for a tax adviser or for any date after 11 June 2034.
records.hypothesis: Velden may provide the pricing schedule to the annual auditor on 11 June 2034.

records.document:
Merrow's FY2035 continuing-operations profit was exactly USD 1.80 million. Continuing operations and discontinued operations are reported separately and must not be combined for this line item.

Merrow's FY2035 discontinued-operations profit was exactly USD 0.20 million. The combined profit from both categories was USD 2.00 million.

Merrow's FY2034 continuing-operations profit was USD 2.00 million.
records.hypothesis: Merrow's FY2035 continuing-operations profit was exactly USD 2.00 million.

records.document:
For the first quarter of 2036, Iskra Instruments' net change in cash was negative USD 125 thousand. A negative net change means cash decreased, not increased.

The same quarter included positive USD 210 thousand of investing cash flow and negative USD 335 thousand of operating cash flow; these two flows are the entire net change.

At the prior year end, cash was USD 900 thousand.
records.hypothesis: Iskra Instruments' cash increased by USD 125 thousand during the first quarter of 2036.

records.document:
The Fenwick covenant requires the debt-to-equity ratio to be strictly less than 0.60. Equality with 0.60 is a breach, not compliance.

At the 2037 measurement date, Fenwick had debt of USD 30 million and equity of USD 50 million. These are the amounts used for the covenant ratio.

For a separate reporting metric, debt was below USD 40 million; that metric does not replace the ratio covenant.
records.hypothesis: Fenwick complied with its debt-to-equity covenant at the 2037 measurement date.

records.document:
Nivara must not publish any reserve report unless at least 3 directors have signed it. A report with fewer than 3 director signatures remains prohibited from publication.

The 2038 reserve report has exactly 2 director signatures. The third signature line is blank, and no substitute signature is accepted.

The 2037 reserve report had 4 director signatures and was published last year.
records.hypothesis: Nivara may publish the 2038 reserve report under the director-signature rule.

records.document:
Yarrow Retail reported revenue of USD 11.2 million for FY2039. This excerpt reports FY2039 results only; it makes no statement about FY2040 revenue.

The FY2039 gross margin was 24 percent, and the FY2039 statement was approved on 20 February 2040.

A new warehouse opened during FY2039.
records.hypothesis: Yarrow Retail's FY2040 revenue exceeded USD 11.2 million.

records.document:
Oridon recorded exactly 8 warranty claims during April 2041. Each claim concerned a distinct unit sold in April 2041.

The excerpt does not state how many units Oridon sold during April 2041. March sales were 400 units and must not be substituted for April sales.

April warranty reimbursements totaled USD 1600.
records.hypothesis: Exactly 2 percent of the units Oridon sold in April 2041 produced warranty claims that month.

records.document:
Under the 2042 inspection agreement, Caldra may hire exactly 2 independent inspectors after obtaining written approval. This permission imposes no duty to hire inspectors.

Caldra obtained the written approval on 6 May 2042. The excerpt records permission and approval but does not report whether Caldra exercised the permission.

The agreement requires Caldra to retain inspection records for 7 years.
records.hypothesis: Caldra hired exactly 2 independent inspectors after obtaining the May 2042 approval.

records.document:
For 2043, the Larkspur East subsidiary employed exactly 240 people. The figure covers only Larkspur East and excludes the parent company and all other subsidiaries.

The parent, Larkspur Holdings, owns Larkspur East and Larkspur West. Larkspur West's workforce is not quantified in this excerpt.

Larkspur East leased 3 offices during 2043.
records.hypothesis: Larkspur Holdings and all its subsidiaries together employed exactly 240 people in 2043.
